impact: Admins can't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Entra ID audit logs.

updates.content:
Title: Admins can't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs

User impact: Admins can't identify who deleted a Viva Engage community or its Microsoft 365 Group in Entra ID audit logs.

More info: Impact applies to deletions initiated from both the Viva Engage web experience and the Viva Engage app in Microsoft Teams.

Admins needing to identify who deleted a specific community or group during the affected period should open a Microsoft support case with the deletion date and group/community details so support can trace the initiating user through service-side logs.

Current status: We've identified an update to our Viva Engage communities that’s preventing admins from identifying users who deleted a Viva Engage community or its connected Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs. We've developed and are internally validating a fix to remediate the impact. We'll provide an updated timeline for the deployment of our solution and the remediation of the impact once it has become available.

Scope of impact: This issue is preventing all admins from identifying who deleted Viva Engage communities or their connected Microsoft 365 Group in Microsoft Entra ID audit logs.

Root cause: A recent update to improve group deletions of Viva Engage communities within Microsoft Teams is resulting in impact. 

Next update by: Wednesday, September 2, 2026, at 11:00 PM UTC
